content:
cheng: Noticed a weird cold-start perf pattern on Llama-3 13B when hidden_stride != head_dim. Latency spike on first ~10 requests and then normalizes.
cheng: Stack traces point to kernel selector hitting slowpath for KV warmup and choosing a memset-heavy kernel for KV tile init.
cheng: Example from instance-42 logs: ```[2026-03-16 09:12:03] kernel_selector: chose kv_init_slow for model=llama3-13b stride=64 head_dim=56 seq=1024
[2026-03-16 09:12:03] kv_cache: alloc 1.2GB, zeroing pages via cudaMemset -> 420ms
[2026-03-16 09:12:03] runtime: first token latency 840ms, subsequent tokens ~22ms```
sam: hmm, stride 64 vs head_dim 56. That's an odd mismatch. Is that from a custom quant+layout?
cheng: It's from our repacked weights (quant 4/8 mix) + new ROPE theta tweak. Model metadata says head_dim=56, hidden_size=7168, hidden_stride configured 64 to align with tensor cores.
priya: Could be an alignment-triggered kernel path: kernel selector has a branch for stride%warp==0 -> fast_kv_init, else slow generic.
alex: I remember we added a conservative fallback in selector v2.9 for non-power-of-two strides to avoid misaligned loads on Ampere. Might be too conservative for these head_dim combos.
zach: Repro steps? I can spin a small repro locally if someone posts the exact model config + a mini script.
cheng: Repro script snippet: ```python
model_config = {"model":"llama3-13b","head_dim":56,"hidden_stride":64,"rope_theta":1000}
# warmup: 2x short prompts then a long 1k seq prompt
```
cheng: Profiling traces show kernel selection decision takes ~2.3ms per batch on cold start and the memset dominates. After first requests we hit cached allocator path and kernel_selector chooses fast_kv_map.
sam: If memset is the culprit, could we pre-touch pages on host and use cudaMemAdvise to make it async? But that changes memory residency semantics for Private customers.
priya: Another option: change selector heuristics — treat hidden_stride >= head_dim as aligned for the purpose of kernel choice. That might enable the tensorcore-friendly init. Risky if hidden_stride is larger but misaligned to warp.
cheng: I prototyped a change: allow stride-head_dim delta < 16 to pick fast path. Local tests: cold-start first token latency dropped from 840ms -> 110ms. No regression on the 70b nightly suite.
alex: Nice. What's the test coverage? We need unit tests for kernel_selector table and a perf regression test for cold-start P50/P95.
cheng: Added a table-driven test and a microbench: `tests/perf/cold_kv_init.py` that exercises head_dim in [32,56,64,80] vs hidden_stride in [56,64,72,80]. All pass locally.
zach: Paranoid check: does this change interact with ROPE theta scaling? If rope_theta impacts KV indexing we might get subtle correctness issues.
cheng: Good call. I ran evals on our chat templates (few-shot + system) across rope_theta 1000/2500/10000 — outputs matched reference within edit-distance threshold.
sam: Can we gate the selector tweak behind a rollout flag (canary)? Push config to dedicated where we can A/B for 24h.
cheng: Yep, PR includes feature flag `fast_kv_stride_tolerance=16` default off. I'll enable on staging and roll to 10% dedicated.
ops-bot: deploy triggered: staging/eng-runtime/kv-selector-tolerance -> success (build 4821).
priya: After canary, watch token-level latency and memory OOMs. Add a tracer that logs chosen kernel name + reason for slowpath so we can correlate.
alex: Also update Optimize docs to include this heuristic note and advice for customers repacking with non-standard stride.
cheng: Plan: finish canary rollout tomorrow, gather 24h slices, then flip on for dedicated if stable. I'll post results in #eng-runtime. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
